title: Integrated pest management — controlled evidence plan
purpose: Define a scouting- and evidence-led cannabis IPM SOP foundation while keeping pesticide selection, application and local action thresholds under current label, jurisdiction and facility authority.

excludedUntilAuthorized: mixing rates, tank-mix recipes or off-label use
assumption that research efficacy equals legal registration
automatic release from quarantine based on one negative observation

claims.statement: Important greenhouse cannabis/hemp piercing-sucking pests include twospotted spider mite, hemp russet mite, broad mites and cannabis aphids, and their injury can affect leaf condition, flower/resin production or other crop outcomes.
claims.boundary: Relative pest importance varies by geography, production system, crop stage and facility history; this list is not exhaustive.

claims.statement: A defensible IPM program emphasizes prevention, scouting, correct identification, sanitation/biosecurity, environmental and cultural management, and integrated controls rather than relying on pesticide application as the first or only response.
claims.boundary: Specific control choices still require pest identity, crop/site status, efficacy evidence, legal authority, label compliance and facility approval.

claims.statement: Scouting data are stronger when they preserve exact location, plant/crop stage, pest or damage evidence, counts or ordinal severity, date/time, sampling effort and repeat observations so distribution and trend can be distinguished from isolated findings.
claims.boundary: A single convenience observation cannot establish facility-wide population level, absence or treatment success.

claims.statement: Pest feeding can affect crop performance and chemical-development outcomes under studied conditions, so apparently localized infestations can still justify timely scope assessment and monitoring.
claims.boundary: The magnitude and direction of crop effects are not universal across pests, densities, genotypes, stages or environmental conditions.

claims.statement: Published hemp russet mite trials show that treatment efficacy can differ by treatment and production context, illustrating why control decisions should rely on current evidence and post-treatment verification rather than assuming a product will work.
claims.boundary: A research treatment is not an operational recommendation and must not be used unless current registration/label, crop/site, worker-safety and jurisdictional requirements authorize it.

claims.statement: In the United States, pesticide product labeling defines enforceable use conditions including site, pest, directions and precautions, so diagnostic confidence does not itself grant authority to select, mix or apply a pesticide.
claims.boundary: State rules, licensing, employer procedure and current product-specific labeling may impose additional or more restrictive requirements.

claims.statement: Quarantine, sanitation state, pesticide restricted-entry status, quality hold and equipment out-of-service status are separate controls and should not be treated as interchangeable release states.
claims.boundary: Release requires evidence for the specific control being cleared; expiry of one status does not automatically clear another.

claims.statement: IPM effectiveness should be verified after intervention using the same or a compatible monitoring method, documented timing and representative locations before closing the event or changing strategy.
claims.boundary: Short-term count reduction does not by itself prove eradication, long-term control or freedom from reinfestation.

requiredNewPackageSections: facility scouting map and sampling plan
pesticide label and jurisdiction verification handoff
releaseGates: current pesticide-label/legal review for operational surfaces
